column1: # One row per check. Mostly a projection of load_checks(): Check already declares eats,
# tests, applies_at, layer and may_block, so those columns are extracted, not measured.
# WITNESS    CORRECTED. An earlier version of this file cited
#            `test_pre_tier_block_invariant` as the witness for all 15 Pre checks. That
#            law asserts each check's `posture` FIELD equals BLOCK. It never runs a
#            check, so it is not evidence that one fires -- the same class of
#            non-evidence as Keel's occasion algebra, and this file was asserting it as
#            a witness. The real witnesses are named per row:
#              * Pre  -- its own file under tests/predicates/, which drives the
#                predicate and pins what it does and does not fire on.
#              * Stop -- test_stop_gate_level_invariant, which fires EVERY live gate
#                through its real .run(ctx), the exact call run_stop_checks makes.
#            Verified by disarming rather than by reading, and the disarm is NAMED so the
#            number is reproducible. Re-measured 2026-08-30 against a 1934-test suite:
#              * illusoryInterruptionClaim -- replace _INTERRUPTION_CLAIM_RX with a regex that
#                matches nothing: 6 tests redden, all in tests/predicates/.
#              * writeThrashRevert -- make `predicate` return None as its first statement:
#            The second read 8 before this re-measurement and nothing checked it, so it had
#            drifted as the suite changed. These are RECORDED measurements, not a gate: no test
#            re-runs them, because two disarmed suite passes cost ~90s on every run. Reproduce
#            with the disarms exactly as named above.
# FIRES_VIA  the edge. Of five allowed edges only Pre and Stop carry any check; Post,
#            SessionStart and SubagentStop admit checks nothing declares, and a check on
#            an edge the dispatcher cannot deliver would load clean and never fire.
